transfer.common_abstraction: A global target is assembled from several locally certified components/sectors, so the aggregation law is load-bearing.
enabling_assumptions: there is a finite component/sector decomposition meaningful for the target quantity
each local component carries a valid local certificate
the map from local certificates to the global target is explicitly typed
disanalogies: C044 is a minimization problem for cover families on disjoint complement components; spectral gap is an infimum over energies in accessible excited sectors
C044 can pay a binary separator overhead ceil(log2 t); a transfer operator has no analogous free separator coordinate
OS reconstruction quotients null vectors and then completes a Hilbert space, so source sectors can disappear, couple, or fail density
a correlation rate seen by one source need not detect a lower-energy orthogonal sector
transfer.cheapest_falsifier: Two-sector positive transfer operator T=diag(q_h,q_l) with 0<q_h<q_l<1 and source psi_h=e_h.
transfer.DifferenceWitness: C044 cover cost aggregates by max local cost plus logarithmic component separation. In the target spectral world the full gap aggregates by the minimum accessible energy, while a non-dense source can see only the faster sector and miss the lower-energy state entirely. Thus the aggregation law and source-completeness condition are not preserved.

exact_model: span{e_h} is not dense in H_exc
